recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If the work group wants a specific OperationOutcome.issue.code for this scenario, handle that as a new decision rather than inferring it from FHIR-7259.
issue_request: FHIR-7259 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core extensibility issue asking that the modifier-extension guidance that told systems to refuse to process data specify the error code and any OperationOutcome recommendations; its resolution was to add an example, and the Jira comment says this was already done.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-7259 was found. The same modifier-extension section was updated by b58cc25916bd7787982d82331cb5654a4b7bc305 / svn revision 6392, which added an example that a server could return HTTP 422 with an OperationOutcome when a client PUTs or POSTs an unknown modifier extension.
additional_context: FHIR-6850 is the same change family and directly requested clarification of the HTTP response for create/update when a modifier extension is detected. Later FHIR-18353 refined the old 'refuse to process' wording so the current page distinguishes processing resource data from simply storing or moving resources, while preserving rejection as one valid handling path. source/fhir.ini maps the Extension type page to extensibility, confirming source/extensibility.html is in current build scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because current source/extensibility.html already includes the relevant example and adding a specific OperationOutcome.issue code now would go beyond the Jira resolution and historical applied change.
